title: Finite finitely presented ring extensions preserve finite presentation of modules
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $S$ is finitely generated as an $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and finitely presented as an $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $M$ be an $S$-module. Then $M$ is finitely presented as an $R$-module if and only if it is finitely presented as an $S$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].

proof.text: The finite module hypothesis and finite $R$-algebra presentation of $S$ imply that $S$ is finitely presented as an $R$-module by the existing finite-algebra presentation lemma. Applying the Mathlib scalar-tower lemma `Module.FinitePresentation.trans` to $R\to S$ and the $S$-module $M$ then shows that finite presentation of $M$ over $S$ implies finite presentation over $R$.

source.place: Algebra Tag 0564, proof: the direction from finite presentation over S to finite presentation over R, together with Mathlib Module.FinitePresentation.trans

proof.text: If $M$ is finitely presented over $R$, the finite generation of $S$ as an $R$-module makes $S$ a finite-type $R$-algebra: module generators also generate the algebra, since every element of $S$ is already an $R$-linear combination of them. The existing finite-type subring lemma (Algebra Tag 0561) therefore gives that $M$ is finitely presented as an $S$-module.
